question.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Constant
question.worked_solution:
For any constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{E}[a]=a.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\text{E}[{c}^{2}]={c}^{2}.
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Scaled Random Variable
question.worked_solution:
For any constant $a$ and any random variable $X,$ we have

$$
\text{E}[aX]=a\text{E}[X].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[3X] & =3\text{E}[X] \\  & =3(-\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Scaled Random Variable
question.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.35$ | $0.15$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[-2X].$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find $\text{E}[X].$ 

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.35+1\cdot 0.15+2\cdot 0.15+3\cdot 0.1+4\cdot 0.25 \\  & =1.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[-2X] & =-2\text{E}[X] \\  & =-2\cdot 1.75 \\  & =-3.5.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Transformed Random Variable
question.worked_solution:
For any constants $a$ and $b$ and any random variable $X,$ we have

$$
\text{E}[aX+b]=a\text{E}[X]+b.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[-2X-4] & =-2\text{E}[X]-4 \\  & =-2(-\frac{5}{2})-4 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
